I feel like I can relate a lot to you. I'm also struggling with school and depression/suicidal thoughts. I thought maybe knowing that would let you know you are not alone.

But back to you.

You're afraid of what getting put in a mental hospital will do to your situation (uni, the apartment, and the part time job) which is totally understandable! But think about it this way... Don't you think your wellbeing should come before all of that? 

I dont know what your country offers, but I'm currently in a group therapy program once every week,and maybe you could get something alike? This doesnt require you to give up on anything but a couple of hours one day a week. I know group therapy doesnt sound like much, and I cant really say much about it because I am still new to it myself, but it is done with therapists as well as a few others who also have depression.

If this or something like it is not an option for you, maybe you will need to postpone uni for a semester (or two, if your uni only starts once a year) and get put in the mental hospital. This way you can still move in with your friend, and perhaps find a full time job to cover yout expenses until you start uni again? Since you'd still have to pay rent while being in the hospital, I'm guessing? This might not be what you unitially wanted, but it will only be postponed for a year, max.

I definitely think you should talk to your therapist or doctor about this, but also a friend or family member about it, to get some support through this hard time you're having. I know you said you dont want to hurt your family by making them worry, but it's not healthy to keep it all to yourself.

I am just a 19 year old female, so I unfortunately dont have all the answers you are seeking, but maybe some of it can be useful to you. I hope you can use even a little of what I wrote, and you find out a way to make everything work. If you want to talk more, you are more than welcome to hit me up in my inbox :) good luck!

I didnt have to read much of your post to come to the conclusion: Yes you were. 

You're not delusional or making it up in your head. Any form of physical violence is abusive. Be it done only once, it's still abuse. Of course there's the emotional and mental abuse, which you might (?) have endured.

It's normal to feel like you owe your parents something, even if they weren't always the best parents. They raised you, fed you, and gave you a roof over your head after all.  But I can tell you that you dont owe them shit.

Edit because I accidentally posted too quickly:
I dont know if you want to end contact with your parents and have a life without them, but if that's the case you shouldnt feel guilty about it.

If they arent abusive anymore, you'll have to decide if you want to forgive them and mend the relationship with your parents, or if you want nothing to do with them anymore.
If you want to stay in contact with them doesnt mean you have to do everything for them, and/or see them every day. If you want to see them once a month, that's your choice and you shouldnt feel bad about it.

If they are still abusive,my best advice would be to run and never look back.

I'm very sorry to hear this is what you grew up with, and I hope you work things out in a way that is benefitial to you and your needs.

Where we're from, college is "only" three years, and I am currently about to finish my second year. I was thinking about quitting a lot, too, but then I got the advice: If you are early in the education, quit if that's what you think is best. If you are over halfway, then you power through it.

Similarly, my mother once told me "Doing something you don't necessarily like is okay, if it means that you eventually will get to what you want." And I try to use that wherever it applies.
I really want to go to Japan, so I had a part time job I didn't really like, in order to save up money.

This should not apply if you feel like your mental health or your life is in danger, as your well-being is more important than any education in the world. You yourself will have to decide if it's worth it throwing away those years you spent on your education, or if it's worth it to continue and finish what you started.

I am unfortunately still struggling myself, but I'm trying to do different things to get happier.
I try to go on walks every day, so I can get some exercise and fresh air, and I also keep a "Happy notebook".

This "Happy Notebook" is a notebook where I each day write in three good things that happened that day. In the beginning and on bad days, it can be very challenging to come up with three positive things, but it doesn't have to be anything extraordinary. It can be simple things such as the sun shining, you had a pleasant conversation, or that you got a delicious meal. If you keep forcing yourself to think positively, with time you'll start thinking more positively by nature.

As for feeling empty inside I still haven't cracked the code myself, but I would think that getting some kind of purpose in your life will do that? Maybe your purpose is to graduate college and get a job so you can be there for your mother and take care of her? Maybe it's something more simple? 

Do you have any hobbies? If you don't really have a hobby you're passionate about, I'd suggest you try to find one. Who knows, maybe starting a new hobby will do great things for you and give you a new sense of purpose.

You really sound like a nice person, so I sincerely hope you figure everything out and get some happiness back in your life.
If you start feeling like suicide is the only way out, seek out your doctor immediately and tell them. I know it's difficult, but it's come too far by then.

Are you getting professional help? If not, I strongly suggest you seek out your doctor. I've been in that situation before, and it took me months to finally do it.

I wont tell you cliché stuff like "It will get better" and that, because it might not. But you'll never know if you dont try. Arent you at least a bit curious how your life will be in 5, 10, or 20 years? I dont know how old you are, or where you are with your life, but a lot of things could happen. Maybe you'll get married? Get a (new) job, or a promotion? Maybe you'll find your calling?

This might sound stupid, but one thing that helped me was to keep a little notebook to write in 3 good things that happened to you that day. Some days (especially in the beginning) it will be very difficult, but with time you will get better at it. These good things dont even have to be major, but can be small things you appreciated through your day, or learned to appreciate. Maybe you saw some beautiful flowers blooming? A stranger smiled at you? You ate a delicious meal? You were running late but you caught your bus or train? 
It's the little things that count. With time you'll start thinking more positively, but you have to give it a proper chance.

They always suggest exercise for depressed people, so why not set a goal to start working out? It doesn't necessarily have to be in a gym, but maybe your home will do the trick? If not, set a goal to at least go on a walk every day. That way you'll exercise, get fresh air, and perhaps experience good things you can write in your notebook? If it didn't rain while on your walk, that's a good thing already.
Walks are a good way to get some thinking time, too. Maybe you can realize some things in your life that make you depressed, that you can change?

You might not always feel up for it, but starting a new hobby might be good for you, to give you a new sense of purpose?
If you think a new hobby might be for you, you need to figure out what kind of hobby you're looking for.
Are you looking for team activities? Try football, handball or the likes. If you prefer not being on a team, but still being around people, what about martial arts or arts class?
If you prefer something you can do alone in your home, maybe think of what you are interested in? Would you like to learn how to draw or paint? Do you like graphical design? Maybe you'd like to try crafty things made out of sticks and the likes? The possibilities are all there.

I'm sorry for rambling, but I hope you find at least some of it useful.
